title: Energy Transfers and Transformations
seo_title: Year 8 Science: Energy Transfers and Transformations Worksheets (Australian Curriculum)
standard_text: Investigate the transfer and transformation of energy, including kinetic and potential energy, and use energy flow diagrams to show that energy is conserved (summary of the Australian Curriculum v9.0 Science content description).
meta_desc: Free Year 8 science worksheets on energy: kinetic and potential energy, transfers and transformations, conservation of energy, efficiency, and renewable energy in Australia. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Energy is never used up, only changed.
key_sub: Energy transforms from one form to another; some is always dissipated as heat.
body_html:
How to think about it

Energy cannot be created or destroyed; it is transferred or transformed.

  • Kinetic energy: moving objects (more mass or speed, more energy; doubling speed gives four times the energy).
  • Gravitational potential energy: raised objects. Falling transforms it into kinetic energy.
  • Efficiency = useful energy out ÷ energy in × 100%. The rest is dissipated, mostly as heat.
Example

A kettle: 2000 J in, 1600 J heats water. Efficiency?

1600 ÷ 2000 = 0.8

Answer: 80%

Example

A dropped ball: which energy increases?

it speeds up

Answer: kinetic

Common mistakes

  • Thinking energy is used up.
  • Thinking kinetic energy doubles when speed doubles (it is four times).
  • Calling heat lost to the surroundings 'destroyed' energy.

faq.q: What is the difference between energy transfer and transformation?
faq.a: A transfer moves energy from one object to another, such as heat from a stove to a pan. A transformation changes it from one form to another, such as chemical to kinetic energy.
Some energy is always transferred to the surroundings as heat or sound because of friction and resistance.

faq.q: How does Snowy Hydro make electricity?
faq.a: Water stored high in the mountains has gravitational potential energy. As it falls through pipes it spins turbines that drive generators.

items.q: What energy transformation happens at the Snowy Hydro power stations?
c: gravitational potential energy of water → kinetic energy → electrical energy
items.e: Falling water spins turbines.

items.q: What is the main form of energy in a book on a high shelf?
items.e: A book on a high shelf has gravitational potential energy.

items.q: Which energy store is mainly filled in a battery?
items.e: Stores: kinetic, gravitational potential, elastic potential, chemical, thermal.

items.q: Which energy store is mainly filled in a hot cup of tea?
items.e: Stores: kinetic, gravitational potential, elastic potential, chemical, thermal.

items.q: Which stores more elastic potential energy?
items.e: More stretch, more stored energy.

items.q: A car's speed doubles. What happens to its kinetic energy?
c: It becomes four times as big.
items.e: Kinetic energy depends on speed squared.

items.q: What is kinetic energy?
c: the energy of a moving object
items.e: Faster or heavier objects have more kinetic energy.

items.q: Where does a bouncing ball's 'lost' energy go?
c: It is transferred to the surroundings as heat and sound.
It stays in the ball forever.
items.e: Energy is conserved but dissipated.

items.q: What unit is used for energy?
items.e: 1 J = 1 kg·m²/s².

items.q: Which energy store is mainly filled in a compressed spring?
items.e: Stores: kinetic, gravitational potential, elastic potential, chemical, thermal.

items.q: Which energy store is mainly filled in a rollercoaster at the top of a hill?
items.e: Stores: kinetic, gravitational potential, elastic potential, chemical, thermal.

items.q: What is the main form of energy in a glowing LED?
items.e: A glowing LED has light energy.

items.q: Which energy store is mainly filled in petrol in a car's tank?
items.e: Stores: kinetic, gravitational potential, elastic potential, chemical, thermal.

items.q: What unit is used for potential energy?
items.e: All energy is measured in joules.

items.q: What is the main form of energy in a diver standing on a high board?
items.e: A diver standing on a high board has gravitational potential energy.

items.q: What is the main form of energy in a cup of hot Milo?
items.e: A cup of hot Milo has thermal energy.

items.q: Which energy store is mainly filled in a moving car?
items.e: Stores: kinetic, gravitational potential, elastic potential, chemical, thermal.

items.q: What is the main form of energy in water stored behind a dam?
items.e: Water stored behind a dam has gravitational potential energy.

items.q: Why is a light globe never 100% efficient?
c: Some electrical energy is transferred as heat, not light.
items.e: Useful output is always less than input.

items.q: If two balls roll at the same speed, which has more kinetic energy?
items.e: More mass → more KE.

items.q: Which energy source is renewable?
items.e: Renewable sources are replaced naturally.

items.q: A light bulb receives 50 J of electrical energy and gives out 40 J of light energy. How much energy is converted to thermal energy?
items.e: Total energy out = total energy in: 50 − 40 = 10 J.

items.q: Ethan observes a trolley with 120 J of kinetic energy. If its mass is doubled but its speed stays the same, what is its new kinetic energy?
items.e: KE is proportional to mass: 2 × 120 J = 240 J.

items.q: Chloe observes a trolley with 200 J of kinetic energy. If its mass is doubled but its speed stays the same, what is its new kinetic energy?
items.e: KE is proportional to mass: 2 × 200 J = 400 J.

items.q: Mei measures a shopping trolley with a mass of 30 kg moving at 3 m/s. What is its kinetic energy? (KE = ½ × m × v²)
Chloe measures a shopping trolley with a mass of 20 kg moving at 3 m/s. What is its kinetic energy? (KE = ½ × m × v²)
Aarav measures a lab trolley with a mass of 5 kg moving at 3 m/s. What is its kinetic energy? (KE = ½ × m × v²)
A ball is dropped. What happens to its energy as it falls?
c: Gravitational potential energy is transformed into kinetic energy.
Kinetic energy turns into potential energy.
items.e: It speeds up as it falls.

items.q: A ball has 40 J of gravitational potential energy at the top of a fall. Ignoring air resistance, how much kinetic energy does it have just before it hits the ground?
items.e: Energy is conserved: all the potential energy becomes kinetic energy.

items.q: Priya observes a trolley with 40 J of kinetic energy. If its speed is doubled and its mass stays the same, what is its new kinetic energy?
items.e: KE depends on speed squared: 2² = 4, so 4 × 40 J = 160 J.

items.q: What is gravitational potential energy?
c: energy stored because an object is raised above the ground
items.e: Higher and heavier objects store more.

items.q: Noah lifts a book with a mass of 2 kg onto a balcony 4 m above the floor. How much gravitational potential energy is stored? (PE = m × g × h, g = 10 N/kg)
Harper measures a skateboarder with a mass of 50 kg moving at 3 m/s. What is its kinetic energy? (KE = ½ × m × v²)
William lifts a bowling ball with a mass of 6 kg onto a stage 2 m above the floor. How much gravitational potential energy is stored? (PE = m × g × h, g = 10 N/kg)
What is the law of conservation of energy?
c: Energy is used up when things move.
Energy cannot be created or destroyed, only transferred or transformed.
items.e: Wasted energy spreads into the surroundings.

items.q: Priya drops a 4 kg ball from 4 m. It started with 160 J of PE. Ignoring air, how much kinetic energy does it have just before it hits the ground?
items.e: All the PE has changed into KE.

items.q: Priya lifts a watermelon with a mass of 5 kg onto a ladder step 2 m above the floor. How much gravitational potential energy is stored? (PE = m × g × h, g = 10 N/kg)
Ethan holds a 5 kg ball 5 m above the ground. How much gravitational PE does the ball-Earth system have (g = 10 N/kg)?
Noah drops a 2 kg ball from 5 m. It started with 100 J of PE. Ignoring air, how much kinetic energy does it have just before it hits the ground?
items.e: All the PE has changed into KE.

items.q: A ball dropped with 80 J of potential energy bounces back up with 60 J. Where did the rest of the energy go?
c: It became new mass in the ball.
It was stored in the ground forever as potential energy.
It was converted to thermal and sound energy.
items.e: Energy is not destroyed: 20 J is converted to thermal and sound energy.

items.q: When a moving object slows down, where does its kinetic energy go?
c: It is transferred to other objects or the surroundings, often as thermal energy and sound.
It stays in the object as speed.
items.e: Energy is conserved.

items.q: Which shows the main energy conversion in a person running?
c: electrical energy → thermal energy, kinetic energy and sound energy
chemical potential energy → kinetic energy and thermal energy
elastic potential energy → kinetic energy of the arrow
items.e: The useful output depends on the job of a person running.

items.q: Oliver observes: “A rolling ball goes onto a carpet and stops.” Which statement about the object's kinetic energy is correct?
c: Kinetic energy is transferred to the ball.
Kinetic energy is transferred from the ball.
items.e: When an object speeds up, energy goes into it; when it slows down, energy leaves it.

items.q: Which shows the main energy conversion in a catapult firing a stone?
c: electrical energy → thermal energy, kinetic energy and sound energy
kinetic energy → thermal energy and sound energy
items.e: The useful output depends on the job of a catapult firing a stone.

items.q: Zara observes: “A football player kicks a ball that was at rest.” Which statement about the object's kinetic energy is correct?
c: Kinetic energy is transferred to the ball.
Kinetic energy is transferred from the ball.
items.e: When an object speeds up, energy goes into it; when it slows down, energy leaves it.

items.q: Which shows the main energy conversion in a hydroelectric power station?
c: chemical potential energy → thermal energy and light energy
electrical energy → thermal energy, kinetic energy and sound energy
gravitational potential energy → kinetic energy → electrical energy
items.e: The useful output depends on the job of a hydroelectric power station.

items.q: Which change shows energy being transferred out of an object?
c: a ball speeding up down a hill
items.e: Slowing down means losing KE.

items.q: A student holds a 20 N bag still for 5 minutes. How much work is done on the bag?
items.e: The bag does not move, so no work is done on it.

items.q: Priya observes: “A football player kicks a ball that was at rest.” Where does the energy come from or go?
c: To the carpet as thermal energy
To the glove and hand as thermal energy and sound
items.e: Energy is never used up; it moves from one place to another.

items.q: Harper drops a ball from 200 cm. It bounces back to only 120 cm. What best explains this?
c: Gravity turned off at the top.
Energy was destroyed when it hit the floor.
Some energy was transferred to the floor and air as thermal energy and sound.
The ball made less energy on the way up.
items.e: Energy is conserved but spreads out.

items.q: Why does a pendulum eventually stop swinging?
c: Energy is transferred to the air and the pivot as thermal energy.
items.e: Friction and air resistance.

items.q: Amelia's ball keeps 70% of its height on each bounce. Dropped from 100 cm, it reaches 70 cm on the first bounce. About how high is the second bounce?
Which formula gives work done?
c: work done = force × distance moved in the direction of the force

items.q: Which shows the main energy conversion in a loudspeaker?
c: electrical energy → thermal energy, kinetic energy and sound energy
items.e: The useful output depends on the job of a loudspeaker.

items.q: Hamish observes: “A skydiver opens a parachute and slows down.” Which statement about the object's kinetic energy is correct?
c: Kinetic energy is transferred to the skydiver.
Kinetic energy is transferred from the skydiver.
items.e: When an object speeds up, energy goes into it; when it slows down, energy leaves it.

items.q: What is work in science?
c: energy transferred when a force moves an object a distance
items.e: Work = force × distance.

items.q: Which shows the main energy conversion in a ball falling from a height?
c: chemical potential energy → thermal energy and light energy
items.e: The useful output depends on the job of a ball falling from a height.

items.q: When is work done?
c: when a force moves an object in the direction of the force
when an object is held still
items.e: No movement in the direction of the force means no work done.

items.q: In a collision between a moving trolley and a resting trolley, what happens to energy?
c: The resting trolley gives energy to the moving trolley.
Some kinetic energy is transferred from the moving trolley to the resting trolley.
items.e: Energy moves between objects.

items.q: Which shows the main energy conversion in a hairdryer?
c: chemical potential energy → kinetic energy and thermal energy
gravitational potential energy → kinetic energy → electrical energy
electrical energy → thermal energy, kinetic energy and sound energy
items.e: The useful output depends on the job of a hairdryer.

items.q: What is the SI unit of energy?
items.e: Work done is also measured in joules.

items.q: What is the main energy change when a pendulum swings from its highest point to its lowest point?
items.e: At the lowest point it moves fastest.

items.q: Is hydroelectric energy renewable or non-renewable?
items.e: Renewable resources will not run out.

items.q: Is solar energy renewable or non-renewable?
items.e: Renewable resources will not run out.

items.q: What is the main form of energy in a ringing school bell?
items.e: A ringing school bell has sound energy.

items.q: How can a home reduce heat loss?
c: ceiling insulation, double glazing and draught stoppers
items.e: Lower bills.

items.q: Is oil energy renewable or non-renewable?
items.e: Renewable resources will not run out.

items.q: What is one disadvantage of wind power?
c: It does not work when there is no wind.
items.e: Reliability.

items.q: What is the main form of energy in a plate of meat pie?
items.e: A plate of meat pie has chemical potential energy.

items.q: A device is supplied with 400 J of energy and transfers 40 J usefully. What is its efficiency?
items.e: useful ÷ total × 100 = 10%.

items.q: Why can no device be 100% efficient?
c: It can be if it is new.
Some energy is always dissipated, for example as heat or sound.
items.e: Waste is unavoidable.

items.q: A motor is supplied with 400 J and transfers 100 J usefully. How much energy is wasted?
items.e: Energy is conserved: wasted = total − useful.

items.q: What is the main form of energy in a charged mobile phone battery?
items.e: A charged mobile phone battery has chemical potential energy.

items.q: Is natural gas energy renewable or non-renewable?
items.e: Renewable resources will not run out.

items.q: A device is supplied with 200 J of energy and transfers 150 J usefully. What is its efficiency?
items.e: useful ÷ total × 100 = 75%.

items.q: A motor is supplied with 100 J and transfers 75 J usefully. How much energy is wasted?
items.e: Energy is conserved: wasted = total − useful.

items.q: Is geothermal energy renewable or non-renewable?
items.e: Renewable resources will not run out.

items.q: Why are LED bulbs cheaper to run than filament bulbs?
c: They are brighter so use more energy.
They have a lower power and waste less energy as heat.
items.e: Efficiency.

items.q: What is the main form of energy in the wound-up spring of a toy?
items.e: The wound-up spring of a toy has elastic potential energy.

items.q: Is biomass (wood from managed forests) energy renewable or non-renewable?
items.e: Renewable resources will not run out.

items.q: Mia's 60 kg brother rides a bike at 5 m/s. What is his kinetic energy (ignore the bike)?
Ruby says a car 'uses up' energy. How could she say this more accurately?
c: The car transforms chemical energy in fuel into kinetic energy and heat.
items.e: Energy changes form.

items.q: Ruby pulls a toy car's spring back 2 cm, then 4 cm. Which launch goes farther?
items.e: More compression stores more PE.

items.q: Jack rolls a trolley down a ramp from different heights and measures its speed at the bottom. What is the independent variable?
items.e: He changes the height.

items.q: Kai designs a marble run. How could he make the marble go faster at the bottom?
items.e: More height gives more potential energy to transform.

items.q: Mei wants to graph how mass affects kinetic energy. What should she keep the same?
items.e: Change mass, keep speed the same.

items.q: Which shows the main energy conversion in a torch?
c: chemical potential energy → electrical energy → light energy and thermal energy
electrical energy → thermal energy, kinetic energy and sound energy
items.e: The useful output depends on the job of a torch.

items.q: Liam models two attracting magnets as balls connected by a stretched spring. Why?
c: The spring shows that pulling them apart stores energy.
items.e: A good model shows energy storage.

items.q: Mia drops a ball from 100 cm and measures bounces of 70, 49 and 34 cm. What pattern does she see?
c: Each bounce is about 70% of the one before.
The bounces get 30 cm higher each time.
Each bounce is the same height.
items.e: About 30% of the energy is transferred away each bounce.

items.q: Mia lifts a 3 kg box to a 2 m shelf, then to a 4 m shelf. How much more PE is stored at 4 m?
Which change would make a pendulum lose energy more slowly?
c: reduce air resistance and friction at the pivot
items.e: Less energy is dissipated.

items.q: Which shows the main energy conversion in an electric fan?
c: electrical energy → kinetic energy and sound energy
kinetic energy of the wind → electrical energy
items.e: The useful output depends on the job of an electric fan.

items.q: When an object speeds up, what must happen?
c: Energy must be transferred to it.
items.e: More KE requires an energy input.

items.q: Is coal energy renewable or non-renewable?
items.e: Renewable resources will not run out.

items.q: Is wind energy renewable or non-renewable?
items.e: Renewable resources will not run out.

items.q: Which shows the main energy conversion in a bow shooting an arrow?
c: chemical potential energy → thermal energy and light energy
elastic potential energy → kinetic energy of the arrow
items.e: The useful output depends on the job of a bow shooting an arrow.

items.q: A ball has 80 J of kinetic energy. It slows to half its speed. How much KE is left?
Is tidal energy renewable or non-renewable?
items.e: Renewable resources will not run out.

items.q: Which graph type best shows kinetic energy for trolleys of four different masses?
c: a column graph or line graph with mass on the x-axis and KE on the y-axis
items.e: Put the variable you change on the x-axis.

items.q: Why does a water tower store energy?
c: Water held high has gravitational PE that can push water through pipes.
items.e: Height stores energy.
